picks.title: The best Paris museums to visit with kids
paragraphs: Parisian art museums are very welcoming to kids — but what does one actually think of these world-class cultural institutions when you’re touring with a little one in tow?

This shortlist mixes headline collections with spaces that invite sketching, wandering, and hands-on moments. Use it as a flexible route: pair Orsay with Rodin on a dual ticket, leave room for a garden break, and treat fog sculptures and medieval moats as the real souvenirs.

activities.title: Bourse de Commerce
activities.description: A former government building turned private art collection — ornate interiors colliding with contemporary work. Don’t miss Fujiko Nakaya’s Fog Sculpture when it’s on view.

activities.title: Musée d'Orsay
activities.description: A former train station turned Impressionist temple, crowned by the famous gold clock. Book a dual Orsay + Rodin ticket to skip lines and keep the day flexible.
activities.location: 1 Rue de la Légion d'Honneur, Paris

activities.title: Musée Rodin
activities.description: Hit The Atelier first — interactive, air-conditioned, and packed with activities — then wander the sculpture garden before and after.

activities.title: Grand Palais — Matisse
activities.description: A Matisse exhibit where the artist’s sketchbook can spark kids to open their own. Worth the stop if the current show is running.

activities.title: Musée du Louvre
activities.description: Start at Le Studio for model sand, sketching, and books, then walk the Medieval Louvre — the empty former moat of the fortress, surprisingly peaceful with kids.

picks.title: A designer's curated Toronto itinerary
paragraphs: This is a design-forward day through Toronto — the kind of route a creative director would sketch for a short visit. Expect sharp architecture, thoughtful retail, and neighborhood texture instead of a checklist of tourist checkboxes.

Walk between stops when you can. The point is noticing materials, storefronts, and street rhythm as much as the destinations themselves. Keep the afternoon flexible so coffee can turn into a longer linger.

activities.title: Art Gallery of Ontario
activities.description: Gehry’s light-filled galleries and Canadian collections.

activities.title: Grainge
activities.description: Curated design objects and quiet browsing energy.

activities.title: Lunch at Quetzal
activities.description: Wood-fired Mexican with a refined room.

activities.title: Distillery District walk
activities.description: Brick lanes, galleries, and slow window-shopping.

activities.title: Evergreen Brick Works
activities.description: Adaptive reuse, trails, and golden-hour light.

picks.title: New York foodies
paragraphs: New York eats are endless, so this list stays opinionated: a tight set of places that reward appetite, patience, and a little neighborhood hopping. Think classics with staying power alongside rooms that still feel current.

Don’t try to do every meal back-to-back. Pick two anchors for the day, leave space to wander into a bakery or market, and let the city’s pace decide whether dessert happens at the table or on the sidewalk.

activities.title: Russ & Daughters Cafe
activities.description: Appetizing-counter legends with a sit-down ritual.

activities.title: Xi'an Famous Foods
activities.description: Hand-pulled noodles and cumin heat.

activities.title: Chelsea Market graze
activities.description: A walkable circuit of stalls and small bites.

activities.title: Lucali
activities.description: Cash-only pizza worth the Brooklyn pilgrimage.

activities.title: Uncle Boons Sister
activities.description: Thai flavors in a lively late-night room.

picks.title: Lisbon, one hill at a time
paragraphs: Lisbon rewards a day that climbs and then pauses. This route stays in the historic core — Chiado, Alfama, and a miradouro — instead of trying to stitch Belém onto an already steep walk.

Start with a tart while the line is still short, then let the hills set the pace. The castle and the viewpoints are the structure; everything between them is tiled walls, tram bells, and a reason to sit down.

activities.title: Manteigaria
activities.description: Custard tarts still warm from the oven. Eat standing at the marble counter on Rua do Loreto before the late-morning queue arrives.

activities.title: Convento do Carmo
activities.description: An open-air Gothic nave with no roof — sky where the vault used to be. Quiet, central, and a better first museum than anything behind a long ticket line.

activities.title: Time Out Market
activities.description: A graze, not a sit-down commitment. Pick one stall, eat at the communal tables, and leave before it becomes a food-hall marathon.

activities.title: Alfama lanes
activities.description: Wander downhill from Portas do Sol through laundry lines and azulejo corners. Get a little lost on purpose; the river keeps you oriented.
activities.location: Largo das Portas do Sol, Lisbon

activities.title: Miradouro da Senhora do Monte
activities.description: The wide view over the castle, the river, and the 25 de Abril Bridge. Arrive before golden hour if you want a wall seat without the crush.

picks.title: A Roma-Condesa day in Mexico City
paragraphs: Skip the historic center for a day and stay in the neighborhoods that actually set the city’s rhythm — Roma, Condesa, and the edge of Chapultepec. Tree canopy, gallery rooms, and a long lunch beat a checklist of monuments.
Move by short rides or a slow walk under the jacarandas. The castle is the one grand stop; everything else is bakeries, parks, and a table you won’t want to leave.

activities.title: Panadería Rosetta
activities.description: Guava rolls and excellent coffee in Roma Norte. Go early — the bakery empties its best loaves before the lunch crowd shows up.

activities.title: Museo Tamayo
activities.description: Contemporary art in a low concrete building at the edge of Chapultepec. Compact enough to finish before hunger hits, with a garden break on the way out.
activities.location: Paseo de la Reforma 51, Mexico City

activities.title: Lunch at Contramar
activities.description: The tuna tostadas and grilled catch that made Roma’s long lunch famous. Book ahead; this is the day’s anchor, not a quick bite.

activities.title: Parque México
activities.description: Condesa’s oval park — Art Deco kiosk, dog walkers, and a full canopy. Loop once, then drift the surrounding streets for bookshops and tile facades.

activities.title: Castillo de Chapultepec
activities.description: A hilltop castle with city views and rooms that actually hold a story. Late afternoon light on the terrace is the reason to save it for last.
